summary.name: Email (Wikipedia article)
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia article explaining how electronic mail works, covering its history, message format, delivery process, and the protocols (SMTP, POP3, IMAP) behind it.
use_cases: learning email header and body structure
researching email protocols for a self-hosted mail server
summary.what_it_does: The page explains email as a store-and-forward system in which mail transfer agents, delivery agents and user agents move messages between senders and recipients. It walks through a typical delivery sequence using SMTP, DNS MX lookups, and POP3 or IMAP retrieval. It describes the Internet message format (RFC 5322 and MIME), including header fields such as From, To, Subject and Message-ID, and how the body can hold plain text, HTML, or attachments. It also covers the history from ARPANET and 1971 onward and the mailbox storage formats and webmail services in use.
notable: Step-by-step walkthrough of how a message travels from sender to recipient
Covers header fields, MIME multipart structure, and the mailto URI scheme
Historical context on SMTP, POP3 and IMAP becoming the standard
caveats: Page text is cut off before the IMAP section ends
Describes general email concepts rather than a single tool, so it is not a product to install
